steps.title: Apply online for your Canadian study permit
steps.why: Most foreign nationals need a study permit to study at a designated learning institution in Canada, and you should apply before you travel. Study permit applications must be submitted online, whether you're outside or inside Canada — paper applications are only allowed if you have a disability preventing online application or hold an identity/travel document for non-national residents, refugees or stateless persons. Submit as complete an application as possible, since IRCC can't finalize your permit until your application is complete and missing documents cause delays. PhD students should check whether they qualify for faster processing, which can also apply to accompanying family members.
prerequisites: An IRCC secure account (used to pay fees, submit your application and check status)
A scanner or camera to make electronic copies of your documents
A valid credit or debit card
Your local visa office instructions for the country/territory you're applying from
The IRCC instruction guide, read before completing the forms
Answers prepared for the online tool's questions, which generate your personalized document checklist

steps.title: Book and complete your biometrics appointment within 30 days of the instruction letter
steps.why: IRCC collects biometrics (fingerprints and photo) to confirm your identity and help assess your study permit application. After you apply, IRCC tells you to book your biometrics collection appointment as soon as you can to avoid processing delays — you have 30 days from the date of the letter telling you to give biometrics. Biometrics are valid for 10 years, making repeat trips to Canada easier.
prerequisites: Submitted your study permit application (online, in most cases) with as complete a document set as possible, including your UBC letter of acceptance and your provincial attestation letter (PAL) if required
Paid the biometrics fee at the time you submitted your application — otherwise you may experience delays
Received the biometrics instruction letter from IRCC telling you to give your fingerprints and photo
steps.cost: CAN$85 per individual applicant; maximum CAN$170 total for families applying at the same time (spouse/common-law partner and dependent children)
steps.time_estimate: Book immediately; you must give biometrics within 30 days of receiving the instruction letter

steps.title: Book and complete your immigration medical exam with an IRCC panel physician
steps.why: Only physicians authorized by IRCC (panel physicians) can perform an immigration medical exam (IME), and you must be in good health to be admitted to Canada when you arrive on a study permit. Booking early matters because you cannot use your own family doctor unless their name appears on IRCC's panel physician list, and results must be routed to the office processing your application.
prerequisites: Study permit application submitted (or IRCC medical instructions received) so you know which visa office is processing your file
Valid passport or travel document to present to the panel physician
Use IRCC's list of panel physicians to find an authorized doctor — you may choose one anywhere in the world; your family doctor cannot do the exam unless listed
Tell the panel physician where your application will be processed so results are sent to the correct office

If you genuinely cannot access a panel physician, note that only IRCC's Migration Health Branch can authorize a non-panel physician (dispensation), and this applies to in-Canada applicants in exceptional circumstances
steps.cost: Paid by you directly to the panel physician; fees vary from one doctor to another
steps.time_estimate: Plan for a single clinic appointment plus processing/transmission time — book well before your intended travel date

steps.title: Pay your Winter Session tuition and fees from abroad
steps.why: Term 1 tuition fees for Winter Session are due September 9, 2026 — this first instalment covers tuition for Term 1 courses, the first half of two-term courses, and most student fees. Paying from outside Canada takes extra lead time for funds to clear, so plan the transfer well before the deadline to avoid late fees.
prerequisites: Accepted your offer of admission and paid the $3,000 acceptance deposit (for students on a study permit) through the Applicant Service Centre
Registered for your courses so fees are assessed
Checked your assessed fees under "Finances" in Workday (use the UBC cost estimator beforehand for an estimate)
steps.cost: Varies by program — see your assessed fees in Workday; international students are also charged a temporary iMED medical insurance fee of $237 ($338 for one-term exchange students) plus a $10.54 direct billing fee when they register for courses
steps.time_estimate: 1–2 hours to set up payment, plus several business days for an international transfer to arrive

steps.title: Prepare your port-of-entry document package for arrival in Canada
steps.why: When you land, a border services officer verifies your identity (possibly using your biometrics) and checks that you meet entry requirements before issuing your actual study permit. Airline staff and officers will ask to see your travel documents — without them you may not be able to board your flight, and if you can't be verified or are found inadmissible, you can be detained or sent back on a return flight. If you pass, the officer stamps your passport and tells you how long you can stay.
prerequisites: Carry a valid travel document, such as a passport — travel with the same passport you used to apply for your study permit
Carry the port of entry letter of introduction the visa office sent when your study permit was approved (it holds the permit reference number used to issue your permit)
Carry a copy of your valid UBC letter of acceptance (an updated LOA plus valid letter of introduction if you deferred your start date)
Carry any letters of reference or other documents the visa office told you to bring
Carry your valid eTA (electronically linked to your passport), valid visitor visa (enter before it expires), valid green card or equivalent proof of U.S. status, or other valid travel document
Bring enough money for your stay — the amount varies with length of stay and whether you stay in a hotel or with friends or relatives
Be in good health and have no criminal or immigration-related convictions
Be ready to convince the officer of ties to your home country (job, home, financial assets, family) and that you'll leave Canada at the end of your stay
Read the pre-departure guide and the Canada Border Services Agency's information and PDF pamphlet for international students
Check the Ebola temporary measures, extended until September 28, 2026
If travelling with children under 18, make sure they have the right documents

steps.title: Apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN) online
steps.why: A SIN is a 9-digit number from Service Canada that you need to start working in Canada, to file taxes, and to access government programs and benefits. As a grad student hired as a TA or RA, you must also provide your SIN to UBC for tax purposes (add it in Workday) — online applications can take up to 5 business days, so applying right after arrival keeps payroll on track.
prerequisites: Arrive in Canada and receive your study permit at the airport or border crossing — international students can only apply after arrival

Confirm your study permit lists a work condition, e.g. "May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186(f), (v) or (w)...", "May work 24 hours per week off campus or full time during regular breaks...", or "May accept employment on the campus of the institution at which registered in full-time studies" — if it doesn't, apply to change your study permit conditions first
Have a copy of your study or work permit and your passport ready; documents not in English or French must be translated
Confirm you are eligible to work in Canada — a SIN alone is not enough
steps.time_estimate: Online applications may take up to 5 business days; by mail up to 20 business days; in person you receive the SIN during your visit

steps.title: Apply for BC Medical Services Plan (MSP) as soon as you arrive
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in MSP to access provincial health care like doctor visits. New residents face a wait period of the balance of the month you establish residence plus two months — so coverage may start about three months after your arrival date in B.C. Apply as soon as you arrive, and get private health insurance to cover the gap. If you arrive in August, your waiting period will likely end in November.
prerequisites: Arrived in British Columbia and established residence
Study permit or other document showing your immigration status
Digital scan or photo of ID showing name, date of birth and citizenship/immigration status for everyone on the application
Marriage certificate, divorce decree or legal name change certificate if your current legal name doesn't match your ID
Private health insurance arranged to cover the wait period
steps.cost: $75/month for students on a study permit ($0 for Canadian citizens and permanent residents)
steps.time_estimate: About 15 minutes to complete the online application

steps.title: Check your MSP application status and plan for the 3-month wait period
steps.why: All people residing in B.C. must enrol in the Medical Services Plan (MSP) to access provincial health benefits like doctor visits. New residents are only eligible for coverage after a wait period of the balance of the month in which residence is established, plus two months — so if you're new to Canada, your coverage may not start until about three months after your arrival date in B.C. Following up now confirms your application is progressing and makes sure you have private health insurance covering the gap. Note that enrolment is completed through the B.C. Services Card, which is how you receive your Personal Health Number (PHN), and that coverage always depends on residency: if you leave B.C. within 6 months of enrolling, you may have to repay your medical expenses.
prerequisites: MSP Application for Enrolment already submitted online, in person or by mail
Your arrival date in British Columbia (used to calculate the wait period)
ID documents used on your application
Private health insurance arranged to cover the wait period, or former provincial plan coverage if you moved from another province
steps.cost: No cost to apply for or enrol in MSP; private health insurance for the wait period is an additional out-of-pocket expense
steps.time_estimate: 15–30 minutes to follow up, plus a wait period of the balance of your arrival month plus two months
